facts.statement: The species Lavocatisaurus agrioensis was formally described in 2018, with an adult specimen designated as the holotype.
facts.quote: In 2018, the new taxon, Lavocatisaurus agrioensis, was described, with the adult (MOZ-Pv1232) designated as the holotype.

facts.statement: The genus name honors French paleontologist René Lavocat, and the species name refers to the Agrio del Medio locality where fossils were found.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the French palaeontologist René Lavocat, while the specific name refers to Agrio del Medio, the locality from which the specimens were recovered.

facts.statement: This sauropod lived during the Early Cretaceous (Aptian to Albian stages) in the Rayoso Formation of northern Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Lavocatisaurus (meaning "René Lavocat's lizard") is a genus of sauropod in the family Rebbachisauridae from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian to Albian) Rayoso Formation of the Neuquén Basin, northern Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: The skull was elongated and resembled the shape of Diplodocus.
facts.quote: The skull was elongate and similar in shape to that of Diplodocus.

facts.statement: Well-preserved skull fossils suggest that this sauropod may have possessed a beak-like keratinous sheath at the front of its snout.
facts.quote: The skull is well preserved for the most part, and it provides further evidence that some sauropods may have had a beak-like keratinous sheath covering the anterior of the snout.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis classifies Lavocatisaurus as a basal member of the family Rebbachisauridae.
facts.quote: In their phylogenetic analysis Canudo et al. (2018) found Lavocatisaurus to be a basal rebbachisaurid.

facts.statement: It is positioned as the sister group to Khebbashia, a clade comprising the subfamilies Rebbachisaurinae and Limaysaurinae.
facts.quote: They resolved it in a derived position relative to other basal rebbachisaurids, as the sister group to the Khebbashia, the clade formed by Rebbachisaurinae and Limaysaurinae.

facts.statement: The animal lived approximately between 125 and 109 million years ago, during the Aptian to Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico hace aproximadamente entre 125 a 109 millones de años, durante el Aptiense al Albiense

facts.statement: Fossil evidence indicates a time range from 121.4 to 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 110.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: The species belongs to the family Rebbachisauridae.

rejected.statement: It was a medium-sized sauropod and one of the few dinosaur species known from the Rayoso Formation.
rejected.quote: Lavocatisaurus was a medium-sized sauropod, and one of the only known dinosaurs from the Rayoso Formation.
